plans.note: The outline skips articles 3, 4, 6, 9, 11 and everything after 12, so a limitation/exclusion of liability article is likely in the unlisted text; read sec-12 first since indemnity and liability caps are usually adjacent, and sec-8 for any Client-only risk allocation. Check mutuality of the cap, the amount (fees paid or payable) and carve-outs for IP, confidentiality and willful misconduct.

sec-12 is the operative indemnity. Confirm TrueLink indemnifies us for third-party IP infringement in the licensed software/Hosting Services and for its own negligence, and that any Client indemnity stays narrow — sec-7 (unsolicited commercial e-mail) and sec-8 (Client covenants/warranties) are the likely hooks for a broad Client-side indemnity.

sec-8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) is the natural home for a restriction on the mortgage or web businesses we may operate; sec-2 may embed a competing-product restriction in the licence grant. Flag only restrictions on Mortgage Logic's own business, not TrueLink obligations.

Look in sec-8 for an obligation to use TrueLink as sole/exclusive host or licensor, in sec-2 for exclusivity framed as a licence condition, and in sec-5 for exclusivity tied to revenue share or fee levels. Preserve our freedom to source hosting elsewhere.

Directional check in sec-5 (Compensation) for any obligation that we give TrueLink our best/most-favourable pricing or terms; an MFN running in our favour is welcome and should not be flagged. sec-8 is a secondary location if drafted as a Client covenant.

Non-solicits are often tacked onto Client covenants (sec-8) or the confidentiality article (sec-10). Test duration, scope (employees actually engaged on the Hosting Services) and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out; a mutual, 12-month, narrow clause is acceptable.

No term/termination article appears in the supplied outline (articles 3, 4, 6, 9, 11 and 13+ are not listed), so termination rights are almost certainly in the unlisted text; sec-2 may make the licence terminable/revocable at will and sec-5 may carry termination fees or unamortised charges. Check whether Client may terminate on notice without penalty and that TrueLink cannot exit mid-term.

Renewal mechanics are likely in the unlisted term article; sec-5 is the place to check renewal-period price uplifts and sec-2 for licence duration tied to renewal. Confirm the non-renewal notice window is not longer than 60-90 days and that pricing on renewal is predictable.

No general/miscellaneous article is included in the supplied outline, so governing law and venue are presumably in the unlisted tail sections and must be located before classifying. Accepted: New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales with courts (not foreign arbitration); note only, not a deviation, if it lands on another US state we can live with.

Assignment is normally in the unlisted miscellaneous article; sec-2 may also make the licence non-transferable, which is the same commercial term — do not flag it twice. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or sale of assets, and that TrueLink has no termination right on our change of control.

Directional review: sec-1 definitions (site content, Hosting Services, data) and sec-2 licence grant are where any assignment or licence-back of Mortgage Logic's content, customer data or marks to TrueLink would sit; sec-10 for treatment of our data as Confidential Information and sec-8 for Client grants. TrueLink retaining its own pre-existing platform IP is acceptable.

sec-2 is the licence grant, read with the sec-1 definitions. Check that use extends to our affiliates and to contractors/service providers acting for us, that the grant is not revocable at will or suspendable without cure, and that permitted-use limits match how we will run the co-branded site.

If compensation is volume- or revenue-based, sec-5 will likely give TrueLink a right to inspect Client records; sec-8 is a secondary location. Test frequency (no more than annual), advance written notice, off-site/remote review of records and TrueLink bearing its own audit costs absent a material underpayment.

sec-7 (Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail) is the most likely source of a per-message or fixed penalty payable by Client; also check sec-5 for late-payment penalties beyond reasonable interest and sec-8 for stipulated damages on breach of Client covenants. Service credits running to us are welcome and should not be flagged.

The outline shows only Client warranties (sec-8); the corresponding TrueLink performance warranty and any 'as is'/warranty disclaimer are presumably in the unlisted articles and must be located. Look for a warranty that the Hosting Services conform to spec and are performed in a professional manner for a meaningful period, with re-performance or refund as the remedy; sec-1 for the service-level definitions it depends on.

Nothing in the supplied outline addresses insurance; confirm against the unlisted articles before treating it as missing. TrueLink hosts our site and handles consumer data, so we expect commercial general liability, errors and omissions/tech E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request — sec-12 (indemnity) is the natural anchor for a new insurance clause.

sec-5 is where any minimum monthly fee, guaranteed volume or take-or-pay commitment would appear, with sec-8 as a possible covenant-style restatement. A minimum is acceptable if we retain a termination-for-convenience exit without paying the unused balance; do not double-flag the same term under T4C.

sec-10 likely requires return or destruction of Confidential Information on termination, which partly covers data return; check the unlisted termination article for exit assistance. We need our site content and customer data returned in a usable format plus reasonable migration assistance at agreed rates, and no hostage/hold-back of data for disputed fees.
